# A Dart VM Service session, one frame per line, in the order they cross the wire.
#
# Format (mirrors the line-per-frame convention of flutter-run-lifecycle.txt,
# adapted because this protocol is bidirectional):
#
#   > {...}   a frame the client sends   (JSON-RPC request)
#   < {...}   a frame the server sends   (JSON-RPC response, matched by id)
#   ! {...}   a frame the server pushes  (streamNotify, unsolicited)
#
# `#` starts a comment line and blank lines are ignored. Ids are the ones the
# client is expected to allocate, in order, starting at 1.
#
# Shapes are faithful to pkg/vm_service's dart_io_extensions.dart: startTime and
# endTime are MICROSECONDS since the epoch, getHttpProfile answers with its own
# server-side `timestamp` (also microseconds) to be echoed back as the next
# `updatedSince`, and bodies come back as arrays of byte values.

# --- attach ----------------------------------------------------------------
> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"getVM","params":{}}
< {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"type":"VM","name":"vm","isolates":[{"type":"@Isolate","id":"isolates/1963006521159535","name":"main","number":"1963006521159535"}]}}

# dart:io's extension is registered lazily: the first enable can lose the race
# and come back -32601. The client is expected to retry once.
> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"ext.dart.io.httpEnableTimelineLogging","params":{"isolateId":"isolates/1963006521159535","enabled":true}}
< {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"error":{"code":-32601,"message":"Method not found","data":{"details":"ext.dart.io.httpEnableTimelineLogging"}}}
> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"ext.dart.io.httpEnableTimelineLogging","params":{"isolateId":"isolates/1963006521159535","enabled":true}}
< {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"result":{"type":"HttpTimelineLoggingState","enabled":true}}

> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"streamListen","params":{"streamId":"Isolate"}}
< {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"result":{"type":"Success"}}

# --- poll 1: two finished requests and one still in flight -------------------

# --- poll 2: updatedSince is the previous poll's own timestamp ---------------
# The in-flight request comes back updated (now with an endTime), and a fourth
# one failed at the transport level, so it has an error and no response.

# --- hot restart: the old isolate goes, a fresh one becomes runnable ---------
! {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"streamNotify","params":{"streamId":"Isolate","event":{"type":"Event","kind":"IsolateExit","isolate":{"type":"@Isolate","id":"isolates/1963006521159535","name":"main"}}}}
! {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"streamNotify","params":{"streamId":"Isolate","event":{"type":"Event","kind":"IsolateStart","isolate":{"type":"@Isolate","id":"isolates/7215544120983311","name":"main"}}}}
! {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"streamNotify","params":{"streamId":"Isolate","event":{"type":"Event","kind":"IsolateRunnable","isolate":{"type":"@Isolate","id":"isolates/7215544120983311","name":"main"}}}}

# The client enables logging on the new isolate, and polls it from scratch --
# it has its own profile buffer, so no updatedSince carries over.
